_comment: Stage 0.7 stopwords, split by why they are noise.
The hard rule from the spec: do NOT remove domain-bearing words such as
'blood pressure' from 'blood glucose'. Those live in 'keep_always' below,
which is applied as a veto over every other list, so no future edit can
'corpus_adaptive' words are only dropped when they exceed the
stopword_corpus_threshold in the config (default 0.8 = present in 80%+ of
the batch being mapped) — the spec's 80% rule.
_temp_comment: 'temp' is NOT a stopword. In an ETL schema it can mean 'temporary', but in
a clinical column name it almost always means temperature — and treating
it as noise stripped the only content from 'temp_c'. It is an abbreviation
_instrument_boilerplate_comment: Applied to the QUERY only, never to a concept name — see
Preprocessor.concept_tokens. These words are noise in a survey export's
item text but meaning in a concept name: stripping them made 'Height
above average' and 'General finding of height' tokenize to exactly
{height}, so both scored a perfect Jaccard 1.0 against the column
'height' while the correct 'Body height' scored LOWER for carrying the
extra word 'body'. A finding about a variable outranked the variable.
Questionnaire scaffolding. A survey export's item text is mostly
instructions — 'Tick the one response which best describes your usual
abilities over the past week' — and every one of those tokens dilutes
both the FTS query and the Jaccard union without ever distinguishing one
concept from another. Note 'ability' is NOT here: 'Ability to walk' is a
_question_word_comment: Question and quantifier words matter more than they look. A description
like 'how tall the patient is' left 'how' in the token set, so Stage 2
searched for concepts containing 'how' AND 'tall' — and 'Body height',
sharing no token with the query, never entered the shortlist at all.
Stage 5 can only rerank what Stage 2 found, so no embedding model can
Personal and possessive pronouns are deliberately NOT here, though the
argument for adding them looks identical. Postgres already drops them,
so Stage 2 is unaffected either way; what changes is Stages 3 and 4.
Adding you/your/my/their cost 2 agreed-on-meaning and 2 more unmapped
columns on the 206-column curated set, because a questionnaire item
('Are you able to shampoo your hair') matches a questionnaire concept
partly ON those pronouns — question shape is real signal when both
sides are questions. They are harmless in Stage 3 now that a stopword
is weighted 0 rather than as the rarest token in the corpus.
